fidelity: F2a — Physics-Lumped Single-Diode + Lumped Thermal ODE
description: De Soto 5-parameter single-diode model solved analytically via Lambert-W (with Newton root-find fallback) for the full I-V/P-V curve, coupled to a 0D lumped-capacitance thermal ODE (scipy.solve_ivp). Adds CdTe spectral response and an empirically-corrected, low temperature coefficient. Preserves the F1b CdTe tempco correction factor 0.578.
source: De Soto, Klein & Beckman (2006) Solar Energy 80(1) 78-88; Jain & Kapoor (2004) Sol. Energy Mater. Sol. Cells 81 269-277 (Lambert-W I-V); Faiman (2008) Prog. Photovolt. 16(4) 307-315 (thermal); Strevel, Trippel & Gloeckler (2012) Prog. Photovolt. 20(1) 6-11 (CdTe field tempco); Nann & Emery (1992) Sol. Energy Mater. Sol. Cells 27 189-216 (spectral); First Solar Series 6 datasheet (2019)

gamma_pmp.note: Measured CdTe Pmp tempco -0.28 %/K — far lower than c-Si (~-0.40 %/K), key CdTe advantage in hot climates

desoto_params.description: De Soto 5-parameter single-diode coefficients at STC (1000 W/m2, 25 C, AM1.5G)
desoto_params.source: Fitted from First Solar Series 6 datasheet specs

I_o_ref.note: Diode saturation current at STC (low: wide 1.45 eV bandgap)

a_ref.note: Modified ideality factor n*Ns*k*T/q at STC

tempco_correction.description: CdTe-specific empirical Pmp tempco correction (preserved from F1b). De Soto I_o scaling over-predicts CdTe thermal sensitivity (-0.485 %/K) vs measured -0.28 %/K because CdTe's near-optimal 1.45 eV bandgap suppresses sub-bandgap thermal excitation present in Si (1.12 eV).

gamma_pmp_desoto_approx.note: Tempco of bare De Soto model (numerically differentiated dPmp/dT at STC)

gamma_pmp_empirical.note: Measured CdTe tempco, First Solar datasheet

correction_factor.note: alpha_corr = |gamma_empirical/gamma_desoto| = 0.0028/0.00485 = 0.578. CdTe-ONLY — never apply to Si. Validated vs Strevel et al. (2012) DOI:10.1002/pip.1209.

spectral.description: CdTe spectral / low-light response. Effective irradiance gain relative to the broadband sensor varies with air mass; CdTe's blue-rich response slightly favours high-AM (cloudy/morning) spectra, giving better real-world energy yield than its STC rating suggests.
spectral.source: Nann & Emery (1992); Huld & Amillo (2015) Energies 8 5159-5181 (CdTe outdoor spectral gain)

M_low_light_gain.note: Peak fractional efficiency uplift at very low irradiance (200 W/m2) from reduced relative Rsh/series losses and favourable diffuse spectrum (CdTe field range 1-3%). Applied with a quadratic ramp so it is concentrated at genuinely low light and decays to ~0 by mid-range.

AM_ref.note: Reference air mass for spectral mismatch M=1

thermal.description: 0D lumped-capacitance thermal ODE: C_th dT/dt = alpha*G*A - (1-eta_el)... net = Q_abs - P_elec - Q_conv - Q_rad.
thermal.source: Faiman (2008); Jones & Underwood (2001) Sol. Energy 70(4) 349-359 (PV thermal capacitance)

C_thermal.note: Module lumped heat capacity (~8.5 kJ/(m2.K) glass-glass laminate x 2.475 m2)

alpha_abs.note: Solar absorptance of module front surface

U_const.note: Faiman U0 constant wind-independent heat-loss coefficient

valid_ranges.note: STC = 1000 W/m2, 25 C cell temperature, AM1.5G
